title: Efficacious of itself: infallibly, insuperably, indeclinably
source_text: XXXVII. Inde est quod gratiam illam dicunt esse efficacem per se, id est, talem quae vi sua movet & determinat liberum arbitrium: idque, ut ipsi loquuntur, infallibiliter, insuperabiliter, indeclinabiliter: quoniam fieri non potest ut voluntas humana illam effectu suo frustretur, obstetque ne praestet illud ad quod proprie a Deo donatur; propterea quod haec divina gratia omnem hominis resistentiam vincit, & vis ejus in eo consistit, ut homo fiat ex nolente volens.
pass_a_gloss: XXXVII. Hence it is that they say that grace is efficacious by itself, that is, such as by its own force moves and determines free choice: and that, as they themselves speak, infallibly, insuperably, indeclinably: since it cannot be that the human will frustrate it of its effect, and hinder that it perform that for which it is properly given by God; because this divine grace overcomes all resistance of man, and its force consists in this, that man becomes from unwilling willing.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXVII. That is why they call this grace efficacious of itself, that is, grace that by its own force moves and determines free choice, and does so, in their own words, 'infallibly, insuperably, indeclinably'. For the human will cannot cheat it of its effect or prevent it from accomplishing what God properly gives it for, because this divine grace overcomes all human resistance, and its power consists in making a person willing who was unwilling.

lemmas.latin: ut homo fiat ex nolente volens
lemmas.gloss: that man becomes from unwilling willing

choices.why: Kept as in I-XXX: grace whose efficacy comes from the grace itself, not from the consent that follows.
